title: Plan M: AI Learning / Paper Reading Workflow
summary: Define the goal → gather materials → AI deep reading → active quizzing → knowledge base → spaced review
scenario: Best for exam prep, skill acquisition, close reading of papers and building a knowledge system — turning 'read a lot' into 'actually learned'.

steps.title: Define the learning goal
steps.detail: Turn 'I want to learn X' into a testable goal: 'after this I can explain / build / answer what'. Have the AI break the big goal into a knowledge checklist with priorities.
steps.tips: Reverse-engineer what to learn from 'what you should be able to produce' — more focused than marching through a textbook.

steps.title: Gather materials
steps.detail: Find surveys, tutorials, papers and primary sources; use AI search to quickly judge which materials are worth close reading and drop outdated or low-quality ones.
steps.tips: Read 2-3 surveys/intros to build the framework first, then go deep on specific papers.

steps.title: AI deep reading
steps.detail: Feed the whole paper/long text to the model: extract the core thesis, method, findings and key concepts, and surface the terms you must tackle one by one.
steps.tips: Ask for Socratic-style guidance — have it quiz you instead of handing over the answer.

steps.title: Active quizzing
steps.detail: Active recall beats rereading: have the AI quiz you (MCQ / short answer / applied), and go back to the source on mistakes. Use Feynman — explain it to the AI and let it poke holes.
steps.tips: Ask for variant questions on your persistent weak spots for maximum mistake-book effect.

steps.title: Knowledge base
steps.detail: Write what you understand in your own words as 'concept card + links'; have the AI reorganize scattered notes into a structured knowledge map.
steps.tips: Notes exist for quick recall, not transcription; each card carries one line — 'what I can use this for'.

steps.title: Spaced review
steps.detail: Turn weak points into flashcards and review on a spaced schedule; have the AI run a weekly comprehensive quiz to check overall mastery.
steps.tips: Spaced repetition (day 1 / 3 / 7) sticks far better than cramming; twenty minutes a week is enough.

pitfalls.title: Reading summaries, not sources
pitfalls.detail: AI summaries are a map, not the territory; go back to the original for key passages or your understanding stays shallow.

pitfalls.title: Passive reading
pitfalls.detail: Highlighting isn't learning; replace 'reading through once' with quizzing and Feynman-style recall.

pitfalls.title: Notes you never revisit
pitfalls.detail: Notes that go stale are wasted effort; fold them into the spaced-review loop.

pitfalls.title: Unverified AI answers
pitfalls.detail: The model can state wrong concepts or fabricate citations; cross-check key claims against sources.
